newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.05 pct as mini-band lowered.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.05 pct as mini-band lowered.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.05 percent to close at 1.0191 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency of 1.019 to 1.024 per dollar, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new trading level for the fluctuation of the real by buying dollars at 1.019 real and selling at 1.024 reais in a auction before the opening.
The previous mini-band, set on September 10, was between 1.018 and 1.023 reais to the dollar.
In the afternoon the Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0190 reais per greenback to drain excess dollars from the market.
Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Tuesday surplus of around $60 million in late afternoon, dealers added.
In the interbank floating rate market, the real dropped 0.08 percent to end at 1.0248 to the dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed at 1.037 per greenback, down 0.1 percent, traders said.
